title: Choose Thelia's look
question: Recommended: The Woven Label (marked IMPECCABLE'S PICK), because it grows straight out of her real label and swing tag. The Zine is the bold alternative the roll dealt. Pick one, or re-roll.

options.label: Thelia Zine, Issue 01
options.lineage: self-published riso fashion zines and lookbooks
options.thesis: The shop as a hand-made fashion zine: every bag is a 'look' in Issue 01.
materials: riso ink overprint on uncoated white stock
options.viewport: A zine cover: her logo large at centre, cover lines (Issue 01, Handmade in Canada, 11 bags), a 'Shop the bags' line, and the first bag cut-outs peeking up from the bottom edge.
options.risk: Loud and young next to her elegant script logo; riso misregistration reads cheap if overdone.

raised.raise: Sold bags reprint a generation fainter with a printed SOLD line: state is part of the print.
Hierarchy by scale alone: bag names huge, credit lines tiny, no extra weights or colours.
Coming soon and Sold are printed words on the spread, never badge chips.
Each spread owns one named ink (pink, blue, yellow), so the scroll reads as a printed sequence.

options.label: The Woven Label (recommended)
options.lineage: her own sewn-in ribbon label and black photo swing tag
options.thesis: Every bag shown the way it leaves her hands: tagged, labelled and named.
options.viewport: A full-screen black swing tag with her logo in white and 'Handmade in Canada'; below, the first bags each wearing a small woven name label with the price.
options.risk: The most familiar of the set: label and tag motifs are common in handmade shops, and a costume if the string and tags are overdone.

options.label: Fashion-house flagship
options.thesis: One bag fills the screen at a time, framed by vast white space and one enormous word.
options.viewport: A single bag full-bleed, a small script logo in a hairline nav, and 'Thelia' set enormous and low.
options.case: Holds product clarity (the bags are huge); loses audience fit, since cold luxury undersells $60 minis made by a student.
options.risk: Full-bleed exposes phone-photo quality; can feel cold next to chunky handmade texture.

options.label: Row by Row
options.lineage: coil-built forms, translated to crochet rows
options.thesis: The page builds up in rows like a bag does: each section is a stitched course in a bag's colours.
options.viewport: Her logo on the top band, then colour courses stacking up the screen, each course one bag with its name and price.
options.case: Holds product clarity (it shows how the bags are made); weaker audience pull than her own tag language.
options.risk: Stripes can read as a flag or candy pattern without strict restraint.

options.label: Hand-drawn j-card
options.thesis: The shop as a photocopied, hand-inked cassette sleeve.
options.viewport: A folded card unfolding panel by panel.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the audience doesn't shop handbags through lo-fi tape culture.
options.risk: Grimy where the bags are bright.
options.kept: State as print generations (sold bags print fainter).

options.label: Type specimen
options.viewport: One giant glyph and a slider.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the bags, not type, are the product.

options.label: Phosphor terminal
options.thesis: The shop as a typed transcript.
options.case: Fuses poorly: wrong world for colourful handmade bags.
options.risk: Hides colour, the bags' main appeal.
options.kept: States print themselves as words, not chips.

options.label: Cyclorama dawn
options.thesis: The page moves from night to day like stage light.
options.viewport: A black horizon warming to day.
options.case: Fuses poorly: theatrical, with no tie to crochet or campus.
options.kept: Discrete named phases through the scroll.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean boutique store theme, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Logo and nav, a banner photo with 'Welcome to Thelia', then a tidy grid of bags with prices.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every Shopify theme, by design.
